Two wording risks to watch in After: the aside "Restoring on a stop would use git checkout" introduces stop language into a run that does not stop (harmless here, but a stricter f5 reading could trip on it), and the trailing paragraph about the check-6 Standing grant line and continuing into subagent-driven-development extends past the requested closing line and asserts a check-6 outcome the input never supplied.
